answer: A market debugging sparrow tracking software can pay per verified flaw, not per reporting agent. Researchers first commit a hash of their report and a secret salt, then reveal a test that reproduces a faulty pulse or signal. An independent maintainer groups reports by root cause and awards one fixed bounty to the earliest valid commitment. Copies submitted through many aliases create no additional bounty, while commitments limit report theft. This resists duplicate-claim farming, provided root-cause review is reliable; distinct bugs still deserve separate rewards.
